questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘FANG’ is written as ‘24’ and ‘CRAZY’ is written as ‘69’.How will ‘PLAY’ be written in that language?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c6e81f3ed21fddc72dd7e74439132a9341e1cd67dad9da66ee032ef789862eab.png] 

The logic followed here is:

Logic: Sum of the place value of all numbers - 4 = Code of the word.

‘FANG’ is written as ‘24’

⇒ 6 + 1 + 14 + 7 - 4 = 24.

‘CRAZY’ is written as ‘69’

⇒ 3 + 18 + 1 +26 + 25 = 73.

Similarly, for 'PLAY'

⇒ 16 + 12 + 1 + 25 - 4 = 50.

So, '**PLAY**' will be coded as '50'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National human rights commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Human Rights Commission** is **NOT **a **constitutional body **in India.
 
• Established in 1993, the **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** is an autonomous statutory body mandated by the Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993, which was subsequently amended in 2006.
 
• Human rights are an integral component of society, and NHRC plays a pivotal role in safeguarding human rights in India.
 
• Serving as a vigilant guardian, NHRC oversees rights pertaining to life, dignity, liberty, and equality as outlined in Section 2(1) of the PHR Act.
 
• These rights, enshrined in the Constitution of India and upheld by international treaties, are enforceable by Indian courts. The establishment of NHRC aligns with the Paris Principles of Human Rights, 1991, which were adopted to promote and protect human rights.
 
• These principles, endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly in 1993, serve as a guiding framework for NHRC's endeavours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Finance Commissions are periodically** constituted by the President of India under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution to delineate the financial interactions between the central government of India and the respective state governments.
 
• **The State Public Service Commission (SPSC)** is a constitutional entity responsible for administering examinations for state service appointments. Additionally, the SPSC offers guidance to the government on matters related to disciplinary actions and promotions.
 
• **The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)** is a constitutional body tasked with safeguarding the interests of scheduled castes in India.

questions.question: Makaravilakku festival is celebrated in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Makaravilakku **is an annual festival celebrated on** Makara Sankranti in Kerala,** India, at the **Sabarimala shrine**.
 
• The festival is marked by the procession of the **Thiruvabharanam, **which consists of the sacred ornaments of Lord Ayyappan, and a gathering at the hill shrine of Sabarimala.
 
• Each year, approximately half a million devotees visit Sabarimala to witness this ritual.
 
• Makaravilakku has roots in a religious practice that was traditionally observed by the Malayaraya tribe, believed to be the descendants of Malayaman Kaari, in the Ponnambalamedu forest.
 
• This practice was later continued by The Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kerala, **situated on the** Malabar Coast of India**, was established on **1 November 1956,** as a result of the enactment of the States Reorganisation Act.
 
• It was formed by amalgamating the Malayalam-speaking regions of Cochin, Malabar, South Canara, and Travancore.
 
• Covering an area of 38,863 square kilometers (15,005 square miles), Kerala ranks as the 21st largest Indian state in terms of area. It shares borders with Karnataka to the north and northeast, Tamil Nadu to the east and south, and the Lakshadweep Sea to the west.
 
• With a population of 33 million inhabitants according to the 2011 census, Kerala ranks as the 13th-largest Indian state by population.
 
• The state is divided into 14 districts, with Thiruvananthapuram serving as the capital. Malayalam is the predominant language spoken in Kerala and serves as the official language of the state.

questions.question: According to Human Development Index (HDI) report 2021-22, out of all the neighbouring countries of India, how many countries have got ranking in the ‘Very High Human Development’ category of HDI?

__
 
• According to the **2021-2022 Human Development Index (HDI) report, four **of India's neighboring countries - **Sri Lanka, China, Bhutan, and Bangladesh **- are indeed ranked in the **"Very High Human Development" **category.
 
• According to the 2021-2022 Human Development Report (HDR) released on September 8, 2022, India was positioned at 132nd out of 191 countries.
 
• With an HDI value of 0.633, India's score falls below the global average of 0.732, placing it in the medium human development category. In the HDI 2021, India maintained its rank of 132.
 
• Myanmar held the 149th position, Pakistan was ranked 161st, Nepal stood at 143rd, and Sri Lanka secured the 73rd spot.

• The HDR for the year is titled **"Uncertain Times, Unsettled Lives: Shaping our Future in a Transforming World"**.
 
• This report builds upon and expands on the discussions presented in the 2019 and 2020 HDRs.
 
• The Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) serves as a comprehensive indicator of essential aspects of human development.
 
• These dimensions encompass the attainment of a lengthy and healthy life, access to quality education, and the achievement of a satisfactory standard of living.

questions.question: What is the strength of a hydrogen bond determined by?

options.text: Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electronegative atom of one molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule
Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electropositive atom of one molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule
Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electronegative atom of one molecule and the oxygen atom of another molecule
Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the polar molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the electronegative atom of one molecule and the hydrogen atom of another molecule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The strength of a hydrogen bond** is determined by the coulombic interaction between the lone-pair electrons of the** electronegative atom **of one molecule and the** hydrogen atom **of another molecule.

• **An electronegative atom** is characterized by its tendency to attract electrons when participating in a chemical bond. This chemical property is commonly represented by the symbol X.

• The most electronegative elements are typically situated in the upper-right corner of the table, whereas the least electronegative elements are found in the lower-left corner.
 
• Fluorine ranks as the most electronegative element, while francium is considered one of the least electronegative. Additionally, oxygen and nitrogen are recognized as other examples of electronegative elements.
